alt: Table of five assumptions about citizens who gave no answer to the 2020 voting question and the White-Black turnout gap each implies, from the lower worst-case bound through the respondents-only and Census conventions to the upper worst-case bound.

columns.label: What is assumed about people who gave no answer

note: Scenarios are assumptions applied to observed weighted components. None carries a sampling interval, and none addresses misreported votes.

rows.assumption: No White nonrespondent voted; every Black nonrespondent voted
Every nonrespondent in both groups voted
Each group's nonrespondents voted at the rate of its respondents
No nonrespondent in either group voted
Every White nonrespondent voted; no Black nonrespondent voted

source: IPUMS CPS, November 2020 Voting and Registration Supplement; weighted by VOSUPPWT; derived from Chapter 1's components
title: The same file supports a White–Black turnout gap anywhere in a 34-point range until nonrespondents are described
